This study investigates the generalization performance of two-layer neural networks for calculating the ground state of a $d$-dimensional hypercube governed by the Schrödinger equation. Under the premise that the ground state can be found within a specific type of function space known as the spectral Barron space, we establish that the convergence rate of the generalization error is not influenced by the dimensionality $d$. Furthermore, we confirm the validity of this premise through a new estimate that demonstrates the ground state's smoothness in the specified function space, achieved through a proof utilizing a fixed-point approach grounded in the Krein-Rutman theorem. Through theoretical analysis and numerical experiments, we validate that the ground state smoothness is sufficient for fulfilling the prerequisite condition related to the spectral Barron space. Additionally, we show that this condition is non-negotiable through a counterexample involving a specific type of function space known as the spectral Polyak space. Finally, we expand upon our findings by considering the case of calculating multiple eigenvalues, particularly highlighting a discrepancy between the convergence rates of two-layer and three-layer neural networks. Our study's implementation of and analysis results from representative examples demonstrate that two-layer networks can outperform three-layer counterparts under specific conditions. The source code for our experiments is available on GitHub at https://github.com/stracmyr/ground-state-nn. The numerical results in this study are based on the open source library JAX, available at https://github.com/jax-jax/jax. Our study's generalization analysis and numerical results in high dimensions were inspired by the recent works of Li and Li-Neumair (2021) and Jin et al. (2022). To the best available knowledge, our study presents an original analysis for the convergence rates of two-layer neural networks in solving the Schrödinger eigenvalue problem in a $d$-dimensional domain for any $d\geq 49$. Our study also represents one of the primary generalization analysis results for deep learning models in high dimensions. Our study's numerical experiments in the space $\mathbb{R}^d$ for any $d\geq 49$ surpass the existing works of Genz (1992), Liao and Plummer (2018), and Liao (2020). Our study's analysis results for the smoothness of the ground state and the convergence rates of two-layer and three-layer neural networks represent the first efforts in the literature to date. Elegans behaviour on a system-level, opening up possibilities for extended simulations and 'what-if' analyses with the use of synthetic models. Investigating orbital resonances enables the restriction of planetary properties in compact systems. The early K-type star K2-138, hosting six planets, particularly five proposed to be in a prolonged chain of 3:2 mean motion resonances, necessitates the analysis of its planets' potential resonant behavior. By using existing parameters in N-body simulations, our analysis confirms that nearly all simulations (99.2%) produce a chain of 3:2 resonances; however, fewer (11%) demonstrate a five-planet resonance chain. We successfully employ resonances to confine the orbital periods and masses of the planets. We examine the likelihood of this system forming in situ and through disk migration, as well as explore the potential planetary compositions using the runaway gas capture model. We explore the observable signs of the system, including tidal interactions, orbital egg-shaped shapes, and contact opportunities with their host star. The results indicate that K2-138's planets may exhibit noticeable tidal distortions within 50 Myr and could enter a state of close approach and potential gas exchange with their host star in approximately 1 Myr. The limitations of our study lie in its reliance on pre-simulated parameters and limitations in its analytical framework, specifically for its incorporation of tidal heating via l=2 harmonics, which may not accurately capture the actual dynamics. The emergence of this 3:2 resonance chain in nearly all simulations indicates the potential for K2-138 to serve as a prime example of planetary migration in action. The resulting constraints on the planets' properties uniquely position the K2-138 system as a prime candidate for understanding and investigating orbital resonance chains. Audification is a straightforward way to turn oscillatory data into audio, retaining all the original information but potentially making magnetospheric wave observations go by too fast to fully grasp. Consequently, audio scaling techniques used in music have been adapted and tested for ULF wave data, with a discussion that culminates in recommendations for researchers looking to turn these waves into an audible format and an examination of the potential scientific and educational benefits of these novel methods. The author argues that these techniques not only facilitate deeper understanding of ULF wave behavior but also inspire new ways to present these phenomena to the general public. As an example of the potential, the audio files accompanying this thesis contain deep space recordings from the Cluster and Voyager missions remastered for easier listening. By making this data more accessible, scientists can uncover patterns and trends that might have gone undetected through traditional analysis, while also contributing to ongoing discussions on the most effective ways to visualize and sonify these waves in the geosciences. To demonstrate this, the answer to the question 'What does pulsating solar wind sound like?' is explored through the analysis of audioified Voyager data that have been processed using various scaling methods. A new class of rotating black brane solutions, including all possible rotational parameters, have been constructed in an arbitrary number of dimensions. These rotating black branes are flat in topology and exhibit a unique property: when rotation is completely absent, they revert back to original forms of black brane and either planar or cylinder geometries. Despite ongoing research, numerous studies have revealed that a significant challenge in text classification lies in identifying an effective text representation that captures important structural and stylistic patterns.  Inspired by the declaration that our brain utilizes a memory space for storing information, we have introduced the Memory Network (MemNet), a novel, adaptive, and efficient method for text representation.  By incorporating the Hybrid Hierarchical Extractor (HHE) for incorporating external knowledge and making predictions simultaneously, we have enhanced MemNet's capabilities.  Experimental evaluations of MemNet have been conducted on six prominent datasets across diverse categories, and the results show promising outcomes.  Our research indicates that MemNet has successfully addressed the complexities associated with text representation and achieves superior performance compared to established baselines, even without utilizing vast external knowledge sources.  Furthermore, MemNet's computational efficiency and memory-friendly characteristics make it a suitable and scalable option for applications on limited resource devices.  We believe that MemNet represents an significant breakthrough in text representation, and we are confident that it will serve as a valuable building block for developing more sophisticated text classification models in the future. Unfortunately, our model has exhibited less robustness in handling out-of-domain data, and it is a challenge that needs to be addressed through further research in natural language processing.  Nonetheless, we are confident that MemNet has the potential to be adapted and applied in a variety of AI

The advantages and limitations of multicast beamforming for millimeter-wave systems have received little attention in the design of hybrid precoders. To fill this gap, we develop the first integrated design of analog transmit precoders and digital receive combiners for multicasting in mmWave systems, with each device featuring multiple phases and powers. We show that the link layer multicasting gain can be characterized as a Schubert polynomial and that analog precoders can be optimized to maximize this gain. However, the resulting precoder design is challenging, so we relax it and use a partitioned structure to reduce the complexity of power allocation. We also derive the optimal digital combiner that maximally utilizes the receive signal to precision and prove its convexity, enabling it to be efficiently computed via an iterative method that remains computationally demanding. To reduce this complexity, we propose an initial power allocation method that is both efficient and accurate, followed by a simpler solution that trades off precision for greater computational speed. Comparative simulations reveal that the integrated design of hybrid precoders outperforms separate design, while the simpler solution remains highly effective. Moreover, we show that the integrated design can attain near-optimality even with a relatively small partition size. To facilitate hybrid precoder design in practice, we propose a universal codebook that is applicable to different channel configurations, thereby reducing the need for frequent updates. We demonstrate that the proposed codebook design surpasses the existing state-of-the-art in terms of performance. Finally, we highlight the main contributions of hybrid precoder design for multicasting in mmWave systems and outline areas for future investigation. This paper introduces an exact calculation method for worst-case scenario parameter realization in robust optimization problems involving uncertain binary or categorical data. Existing exact algorithms for these problems are computationally resource-intensive, partly due to their increased complexity following reformulation of the problem, and partly due to unknown bounds for decision-independent variables. In contrast, we suggest a Lagrangian dual approach that avoids the increased complexity and takes advantage of the sparsity of the problem, calculating optimal values for decision-independent variables through linear equations and introducing exact dual objectives related to these variables. This approach significantly reduces computational complexity, showing a particular advantage in scenarios with a limited number of decision-independent variables. Furthermore, we apply this method to solve both complete and incomplete knapsack problems in robust optimization and demonstrate its effectiveness in scorable scenarios through numerical experiments. Our calculations indicate that the computational efficiency of this method compares favorably with that of existing exact algorithms, showing nearly a 5-fold improvement in scorable scenarios for a large scale version of the complete knapsack problem in robust optimization. Nonetheless, the method still falls short in scenarios involving incomplete knapsack problems in robust optimization. Consequently, we propose the use of a heuristic algorithm for these cases. Our heuristic algorithm combines advanced optimization methods, including the block coordinate primal-dual method and the variable splitting method, to achieve a computationally efficient solution. Our numerical experiments show that the computational efficiency of our proposed method compares favorably with that of computational methods like dynamic programming and the LMI-based approach in scorable scenarios for a large scale version of the incomplete knapsack problem in robust optimization. Our calculations indicate at least a 3-fold improvement in scorable scenarios for a large scale version of the incomplete knaksack problem in robust optimization using our proposed method. Nonetheless, the method still takes longer to compute than the dynamic programming method in scorable scenarios for a large scale version of the incomplete knaksack problem in robust optimization. Consequently, we propose the use of a dynamic algorithm for these cases. Our numerical experiments show that the computational efficiency of our proposed method compares favorably with that of the LMI-based approach in scorable scenarios for a large scale version of the incomplete knaksack problem in robust optimization. Our calculations indicate at least a 2-fold improvement in scorable scenarios for a large scale version of the incomplete knaksack problem in robust optimization using our proposed method. Our method does not perform as well as the LMI-based approach in non-scorable scenarios for a large scale version of the incomplete knaksack problem in robust optimization.

Our proof methodology employs Shimura's integral representation, which we adapt from Gurevich's approach for $\tau($dy$\rfloor^2)$ as detailed in Theorem 2 of our paper [7] of 2021. Furthermore, leveraging the Siegel modular form representation of L-functions, specifically from Theorem 9.2 of Chandrasekharan's "Fourier Transform and Elliptic Operators' of 1969, the concept of $p$-transposition applies to the p-divisibility of Stieltjes transforms, namely, the Selberg zeta function $\xi_{S}($s,$\nu)$ and its generalizations. The on-center pathway responds positively to the presence of light within its core area but not in its periphery, while the off-center pathway responds positively to the absence of light within its core area but not in its periphery. Our OOCS pathways are developed using a difference of Gaussians, with the standard implementation being denoted as $\text{OOCS-DoG}$, to effectively capture the input's spatial variations. However, this $\text{OOCS-DoG}$ is sensitive to parameter settings and we thus propose the N-OOCS, a more robust and adaptable variant, utilizing a neural network to learn the parameters through back-propagation. The results show a significant reduction in average error rate of $11.17\%$, $14.85\%$, and $5.33\%$ when used in conjunction with the best pre-trained network for these datasets, respectively. However, traditional methods that rely on average operations for calculating prototypes often struggle due to the influence of outliers. This research proposes a new, effective framework that utilizes an episodic prototype generator module to create more representative prototypes from limited support data, reducing the impact of outliers and resulting in preferable models. The framework's ability is further showcased by the substantial improvement it yields over baseline models and the comparable performance it achieves to existing methods on datasets like miniImageNet, tieredImageNet, and cross-domain benchmarks (miniImageNet to CUB-200-2011, and miniImageNet to Caltech-101). Our framework specifically excels on datasets like miniImageNet and tieredImageNet that exhibit significant overlap between categories, by producing more representative prototypes. This is evident through the deployment of our EPG module, which calculates prototypes as a convex combination of data points, in contrast to the simple average used by prior works. Consequently, our framework is particularly effective in learning prototypes with fewer ambiguities. Future sky surveys, notably the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), are projected to observe approximately 10 million time-varying celestial source catalogs daily for 10 years, creating around 10,000 layers of information with over 200TB of data available per year. With extensive tasks and narrow deadlines for object classification within these new surveys, traditional methods struggle to keep pace with rising data volumes and intricate complexity. In particular, Bayesian Neural Networks face significant challenges when used for time-ordered catalog classification tasks due to their computational intensity and limited applicability to real-time data processing. This paper addresses these limitations by implementing a revised Bayesian Neural Network with added dropout layers, which significantly speeds up computation while maintaining accuracy even under tight deadlines. Additionally, we employed noise modeling for the first time in LBNN, allowing for reliable results and accurate prediction outcomes. Results demonstrate a 90% acceleration in LBNN speed with equivalent accuracy compared to earlier studies, making it a viable option for time-varying data classification in big data environments like LSST. Furthermore, we present a newly developed literate programming framework utilizing the R programming language as a useful resource for scientific publications, particularly useful for software and reproducibility-focused publications, such as those using the LBNN algorithm. We illustrate its utility with an accompanying R notebook in the supplementary materials. This updated LBNN algorithm, optimized for speed while maintaining accuracy, exhibits great potential for use in future data classification tasks, particularly in the context of the LSST and similar large-scale data processing centers. Its potential applications extend to research domains in astrophysics, data processing, and associated technologies. We hope that this kind of optimized algorithm and its assessment will contribute positively to the broader research community by enhancing the efficiency of data classification methods, a core aspect of data processing. We present an accompanying validation of the acceleration on in-graph LBNN at the end of this document. Evaluating model performance, the research utilized machine learning metrics, including accuracy, precision, and recall, and found that specific network architectures excelled in different areas: those favoring precision, those with high recall, and those achieving balanced metrics and accuracy. Notably, the study found that restricting models to recent time-series data led to reduced results and suggested that models are incapable of retaining the information necessary for accurate churn prediction over extended periods of time. Furthermore, the study found that individual feature analysis was difficult due to the model's complex nature, making it challenging to determine which factors influenced churn behavior. As such, the study's findings are intended to lay a foundation for future research to investigate specific online gaming variables that contribute to churn. Ultimately, the study achieved successful models that could predict churn in the online gaming industry by leveraging the power of machine learning. As a result, the study's recommendations for implementation are offered to facilitate effective churn prevention in this field. Notably, the study's findings were grounded in collaborative efforts, and the study suggests opportunities for future research to combine predictive models with preventive measures in the online gaming industry. In doing so, the study aims to contribute valuable knowledge to scholars and practitioners alike. Our research shows that lattice calculations can be used to derive transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution functions, with gluons, through large-momentum effective theory. By combining perturbative calculations of gluon TMDPDFs with lattice calculations, we establish a connection between these functions and their equivalents in lattice calculations, involving standard and non-standard perturbative expansions. This work is a crucial step in understanding the structure of hadrons at high momentum and their role in scattering processes. Moreover, it allows us to evaluate various perturbative methods and their effectiveness, given that direct calculations of TMDPDFs on the lattice are difficult due to non-perturbative aspects and complex kinematics. This research demonstrates that using large-momentum effective theory, more than 90% of the TMDPDF's complexity can be removed, making it more accessible for study. Additionally, it allows the direct comparison of different TMDPDF construction methods such as those involving TMD factorization and perturbative expansions. Our results indicate that when applying the method of effective field theories to lattice calculations, the method's main result, a constant function, can be accurately determined with only a few perturbative orders. This is illustrated with our results for gluon TMDPDFs, where we successfully recovered five distinct components using several first few orders of perturbative calculations. This research marks the first successful reconstruction of TMDPDFs, providing valuable insights into their behavior and allowing a more in-depth understanding of the kinematic structure of TMDPDFs, as well as how they can be constructed from lattice calculations. More specifically, our results demonstrate that using large-momentum effective theory, the complexity of TMDPDFs, a function with 18 complex components, can be reduced, allowing a nearly complete reconstruction with only six perturbative calculations. This was achieved with two-loop calculations, suggesting the effectiveness of this method in the reconstruction of TMDPDFs. This research opens up new possibilities in the field, allowing potential further developments and more detailed analyses into the structure of the gluon at a quantum level, as well as its role in scattering processes. With the application of this method, it is now possible to evaluate and compare different TMDPDF construction methods and determine if some are more accurate or effective than others. This research could eventually lead to improvements in the calculation of TMDPDFs, as well as their role in the distribution of momentum in hadrons and their behavior at high momentum. To minimize pollution, bicycle usage is encouraged in many cities, particularly among experienced riders. However, novice cyclists significantly contribute to accidents. A personal health tracker with collision detection capability could enhance safety by alerting users when they engage in reckless behavior. Existing safety technologies such as sensors and video analysis have been effective in preventing accidents, but their potential in preventing non-fatal injuries and minor incidents is still considerable. This study utilizes a bicycle insurance company's video database to train an advanced machine learning model for detecting high-risk cycling environments. By comparing the performance of models built with and without contextual data, we demonstrate the potential of combining various sensing methods and social signals to improve bicycle insurance risk assessment. This innovative approach utilizes video-based analysis and evaluates cycling context risk through testing on two datasets, resulting in significant performance improvements. The technical implications of our research aim to inspire future developments in advanced cycling assistant technologies. The development of this technology can serve as a foundation for creating a smart cycling system that boosts user safety, with potential applications in usage-based insurance solutions. A collection of proper subrings that together form a ring $R$ is known as a cover of $R$.
The smallest possible size of such a cover for $R$ is referred to as the covering number $\sigma(R)$ of $R$,
and if $\sigma(R)$ is less than the largest possible size of an ideal in $R$, it is said to be minimal.
For rings where $\sigma(R)$ is minimal, the gap between $\sigma(R)$ and the largest possible size of an ideal in $R$ is defined as the covering gap of $R$ and denoted by $c(R)$. 
The set of rings of a specific covering gap will be denoted by the symbol $\mathcal{R}_n$ where $n$ is the covering gap of $R$. 
If a specific type of ring has a covering gap denoted as $n$, it is said to be an $\mathcal{R}_{n}$-ring, and if an $\mathcal{R}_{n}$-ring has a specific covering identity, it is said to have $n$-covering identity and denoted as $C_n$-ring.
The specific type of ring $\mathcal{R}_{1}$-ring which contains an identity element is known as $Q$-ring.
The specific type of ring $\mathcal{R}_{n}$-ring which contains $n$ minimal ideals is known as $n$-weakly regular (or $n$-WR) ring.
The specific type of ring $\mathcal{R}_{n}$-ring which contains $n$-WR ideals is known as $C_n$-ring.
The specific type of ring $\mathcal{R}_{n}$-ring which contains $C_n$-ideals is known as $n$-regular (or $n$-R) ring.
The specific type of ring $\mathcal{R}_{1}$-ring which contains $C_1$-ideals is known as $1$-regular (or $1$-R) ring.

To accelerate policy optimization in complex, dynamic systems with multiple influencing factors, reinforcement learning agents can effectively utilize previously collected historical data. Standard experience replay enables agents to retain information from prior iterations and leverage it in future iterations. However, the current approach equally values all collected observations, neglecting their varying degrees of usefulness. To improve upon this limitation, we introduced an experience replay strategy that prioritizes the most informative historical observations more efficiently than methodically collecting new data from each iteration. Our approach is further combined with variance reduction techniques found in importance sampling, enabling the accurate reinforcement of the most likely or desired policy outcomes in complex probabilistic environments. Comprehensive experimental evaluations have demonstrated the novel strategy outperforms existing methods across various high-stakes scenarios, including multiple medical treatment protocols and complex robotics tasks. Specifically, our approach successfully achieved near-optimal treatment outcomes for follicular lymphoma and significantly outperformed state-of-the-art benchmarks by 60% or more in the control of Amazon Cart cart balancing. In this research, we address the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in multi-dimensional space with smooth periodic initial conditions and obtain analytical estimates of the solution's maximum norm, tied to the initial conditions' maximum norm. We also demonstrate that the anomalous dissipation term in these estimates can be quantified. Furthermore, we establish that the force's Lp integrability (with a high enough p) does not enhance the solution's regularity in the Lp norm, indicating a critical role of the non-conservative nature of these equations in this phenomenon. To overcome the challenges posed by integrating periodic functions over complex expressions, we develop an innovative technique for differentiating products of functions and integrate them to derive key estimates. We then use these estimates in reverse to address the issue of whether the Navier-Stokes equations' solution's Lp integrability is a sufficient condition for its continuous dependence on the initial data within the space of periodic functions. Ultimately, these estimates are shown to be convergent under the condition that the initial data's Lp integrability is sufficiently high. Interestingly, the issue of whether the Navier-Stokes equations' solution's Lp integrability is a sufficient condition for its regularity in the Lp norm is closely related to the problem of whether the sum of two finite energy solutions of these equations can also be finite. We address this problem as well, using a technique of perturbing the solution of the Navier-Stokes equations by a suitable function. We prove that if the perturbation's Lp integrability is sufficiently high, then the sum of the two solutions' perturbed version will still be finite. We then remove the perturbation to obtain the desired result. Conversely, we use a straightforward argument to demonstrate that if the initial conditions' Lp integrability is sufficiently high, then the sum of two finite energy solutions of these equations can also be finite. We also extend our analytical estimates and the conclusions drawn regarding the Navier-Stokes equations to a class of generalized models for these equations that involve a Navier-type non-linear dissipation coefficient and are still incompressible and non-conservative in structure. By developing new techniques, the complexity has been significantly improved to O(poly(κ)|C|), which is a substantial breakthrough. Additionally, the developed protocol employs a new form of quantum sampling, known as'repeated quantum sampling,' and is further refined through the application of a classical verification protocol for qubit storage. Notably, the developed protocol solves an open question in quantum complexity theory, and its efficiency has been theoretically matched with a new zero-knowledge proof system, which is of independent interest and establishes a new depth threshold for probabilistic verification of automata. The developed protocol has been rigorously tested and its time complexity has been verified to be O(poly(κ)|C|), which surpasses previous efforts. The accompanying source code has been made available on GitHub, hosted at https://github.com/AlicePleaseWork/ClassicalVerification. The developed protocol's implementation builds upon a number of important technical foundations, including the application of'repeatable' instructions to simulate quantum circuits, the application of 'inner product testing' to detect complex functions, and the application of 'uncomputing' to optimize computational efficiency. The developed protocol's performance has been further optimized for maximum speed by integrating it with the 'Brumley-Lynch' protocol for efficient computation, which is another important contribution of this research, specifically for optimizing the 'inner product' comparison that plays a crucial role in verifying classical results in quantum computation. A blockchain system has emerged as a promising technology to ensure the authenticity and security of data generated by Internet of Things devices, particularly for verifying the authenticity of products and tracking data in supply chains. Despite the potential benefits, several challenges still need to be addressed before implementing a blockchain solution in a general industrial setting. This study aims to highlight various existing blockchain solutions with IoT devices and identifies two primary obstacles to integrating these systems, including the limitations of current research and issues of compatibility between IoT devices and blockchain technology. To overcome these challenges, we present a novel blockchain architecture that incorporates a consensus protocol, oracle services, and suitable data processing methods. This architecture can be applied to update the blockchain ledger local to the node that the IoT device is joined to, thus eliminating the need to send data to a central node. To further address compatibility issues, we also present a solution for integrating IoT devices with the blockchain system, utilizing the Conclave runtime environment. Finally, we demonstrate our architecture and compatibility solution with a real-world application, including a food supply chain, and conduct a thorough evaluation of the transaction count, processing time, and processing power requirements. The results of our evaluation confirm that the proposed architecture is suitable for updating the blockchain ledger local to the node that the IoT device is joined to. However, we also identify a potential limitation of our compatibility solution and conduct a cost analysis to confirm its efficiency. The overall contribution of this study involves the proposed blockchain architecture and compatibility solution, providing a valid and innovative answer to the initially presented problem. The study's results and contributions are further validated through numerical simulations and experimental analysis. A comprehensive review of relevant studies is also provided, offering a high-level assessment of the current state of literature in the subject area. However, atomic interferometry offers improved scalability and more impressive potential for low-frequency sensitivity, even if this comes at the cost of reduced anisotropy. In summary, the use of accelerometers in networks, particularly with the potential of future atomic interferometry-based networks, makes them compelling tools in the global dark matter research search. It finds a strong correlation between polarization and source size below ~5", with a weaker correlation above ~8". The results indicate depolarization due to the host galaxy and surrounding environment. Additionally, the curvature of low-frequency radio spectra shows an inverse correlation with polarization. However, sources with flat spectra demonstrate no such correlation. Lastly, the polarization-statistics correlation is consistent across morphological categories, suggesting an underlying physical link rather than being an intrinsic property of source morphology. It is also shown that extragalactic radio sources make a negligible contribution to foreground noise in current Planck data, while foreground contamination from Galactic sources is more substantial. However, sources from Cygnus A are significantly more prevalent than expected. The polarization-statistics relationship could serve as a means to distinguish genuine cosmic microwave background signals from foreground contamination. The study sets a baseline expectation for counting sources in future microwave surveys, anticipating a higher density of sources than expected beyond ~5". Based on these expectations, the Planck survey underestimates cosmic microwave background fluctuations below ~8', whereas the Planck survey objects of study overestimates by about 10%, primarily due to Cygnus A and similar sources. The study suggests examining polarization-statistics correlations as an alternative method to improve understanding of foreground contamination. The research provides expectations for counting microwaves based on polarization-statistics correlations and the angular size of sources below ~8'. The study offers a new method to improve cosmic microwave background data using foreground correction and identifies opportunities for utilizing polarization-statistics correlations in astrophysical radiation probe design. The study can inform and improves the understanding of polarization-statistics correlations, which has important implications for understanding the interplay between magnetic fields, radiation, and electron physics in extragalactic sources. Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) are a type of mathematical model used to analyze complex systems, often visually represented as a single node with self-loops. These models utilize two key components: a discrete set of states and a set of observable symptoms resulting from state transitions. A crucial factor in HMM analysis is the direction of state changes and available symptom readings at various time points. In this study, the HMM structure is represented as a combination of monads, which are functional patterns with combined effects, to provide a unified theoretical framework for understanding HMM behavior. Specifically, the authors develop an 'abstract HMM' (AHMM) framework to analyze the observable symptoms and symptom expectations, and propose the use of a 'quantitative information flow' (QIF) monad to represent symptom expectations as part of a broader'stateful effects and interactions' (SEI) monad. By doing so, the study provides a clear distinction between explicit, deliberate actions in systems and the inherent uncertainty arising from hidden states, symptom partiality, and time-dependent interactions. Ultimately, the AHMM framework is illustrated with a concrete example of an online advertisement algorithm used by an Israeli stalking app, with implications for extending the SEI and QIF monads to analyze similar scenarios in a more general context. A working Haskell prototype of the study can be found on the related GitHub page at https://github.com/janisvernim/abstract-hmm. These theories are also applied to explain the behavior of particles moving through turbulent flows and may have implications for understanding how particles interact with turbulent flows at the microscale, particularly in relation to biological processes and molecular physics. Protecting users of location-based services with significant privacy requirements is extremely difficult when multiple locations are shared within a short time frame due to the significant relationships anticipated between these locations. Our proposed R\'enyi divergence based framework measures and bounds privacy losses resulting from shared locations, and it effectively addresses a critical issue arising in the analysis of any distribution, notably the significant error in privacy quantification that occurs when conditional distributions are approximated with Gaussian mixtures. Our investigation applies these concepts to a repeated location visit problem, which, from a privacy perspective, is equivalent to a sequence of geometric distributions. This problem is then extended to a broader scenario where repeated locations are interwoven with irregularly visited points, resulting in new challenges that need to be addressed, such as characterizing the geometric distribution and developing a novel approximation that can effectively preserve user privacy. Our research demonstrates that R\'enyi divergence-based privacy quantification can be computationally efficiently realized with this new scenario. Our analysis also shows that a novel approximation that simplifies R\'enyi divergence calculations can be effectively applied, which maintains a small error consistent with the distribution approximation. When using this approximation, R\'enyi divergence-based privacy quantification can be performed efficiently with a computational complexity that is almost linear relative to the length of the location history. Our theoretical findings are further supported by a series of numerical experiments that demonstrate that R\'enyi divergence-based privacy quantification can effectively predict and optimize privacy losses in the context of the repeated location problem. Our research also reveals that R\'enyi divergence-based privacy quantification can be effectively applied to a more realistic scenario where the sequence of locations is interwoven with irregularly visited points, which is further supported by numerical experiments. Although R\'enyi divergence-based privacy quantification does not rely on any parameter estimation, which is significantly different from other approaches, we have also investigated the applicability of heavy-tailed and location-scale distributions that can be fitted with a short sequence of locations using a stochastic maximum likelihood estimator. Our research reveals that these heavy-tailed distributions can effectively describe the significant geometric distribution issue and provide a satisfactory error rate, which is further illustrated by numerical experiments. With these well-fitted heavy-tailed distributions, we have also investigated the applicability of an approximation that simplifies R\'enyi divergence-based privacy quantification, which further demonstrates its effectiveness. Our research finds that heavy-tailed distributions can effectively achieve a satisfactory error rate, which further demonstrates their effectiveness in applying R\'enyi divergence-based privacy quantification. The presented research introduces the NDT-Transformer approach, enabling real-time, large-scale place recognition using 3D point clouds. The technique utilizes 3D point clouds, translating 3D Normal Distribution Transform (NDT) cells into 1D cell signatures via a Transformer network, which are subsequently compared to a pre-built database. The NDT-Transformer outperforms several established methods in terms of recall rate, with an exceptional 88.5% of repeats detected at 10 meters while processing frames at 20 Hz on a single NVIDIA GPU. The research presents a performance and processing overview, accompanying the implementation with an open-source repository. Furthermore, the presented methodology serves as an innovative model for 3D-based place recognition. In a single-hop beeping network, stations interact via one-bit messages to form a distributed communication system. We explore the distributed computing domain's two core challenges, naming and counting issues, and focus on developing efficient algorithms to solve them under energy constraints. Our key contributions lie in creating optimal algorithms for solving naming and counting problems under the survival energy model, where each unit task incurs a constant energy cost, leading to a total cost proportional to the execution time. We also establish the lower bounds for these problems under the partial energy model, where each unit task incurs an increasing energy cost with execution time. We show that the current algorithms are optimal for the survival energy model and that the newly developed algorithms outperform the previous best solutions in terms of execution time while still meeting the required accuracy under the partial energy model. Furthermore, we show that our new counting algorithm has the added benefit of being optimal in the partial energy model as well. Our results significantly improve current state-of-the-art algorithms in various scenarios. We also extend the counting algorithm to solve the optimal $k$-element identification problem, which has key applications in various beeping network problems. We create new optimal algorithms for solving the element uniqueness, top-$k$ element identification, and exact $k$-element identification problems in different scenarios. Additionally, we develop new algorithms to solve the $k$-element identification problem with reduced execution time while maintaining the required accuracy, though the optimality is not ensured in this case. Our work has significant implications in reducing execution time and solving the problem efficiently under different scenarios. We also recover the optimal naming algorithm as a special case of the general $k$-element identification problem solution. Our work along with the given examples and simulations demonstrate that the newly developed algorithms are highly effective in solving the challenges efficiently. Recent studies have demonstrated that languages blended from different origins, 
such as English-Spanish or English-Mandarin, found widespread use on social media, 
though encoding schemes often fail to account for the complexities of code-mixed 
languages resulting from code-switching. This paper presents a dynamic encoding 
approach called PESTO that tackles positioning variability in code-switched 
sentences. Peak switching points estimated for each text are used to positionally 
encode segments based on their language of origin. To improve the method's 
generalizability, no annotated data on language identification or accurate 
sentence segmentation are required. Instead, it relies on predicted results from 
existing models. The approach's effectiveness is validated through experiments on 
code-mixed text classification tasks and comparative studies with default 
encodings, yielding significant improvements in performance. The study's code can 
be accessed at https://github.com/indya78/PESTO on GitHub. For thoroughness, 
interdisciplinary experimental results are detailed in the supplement. $\boxed{}$ 
Disclaimer: This work is an extended version of a recently published paper at LREC 
2022, with added contributions of proposed Peak Switching Points based 
 positional encoding and comparative studies with default positional encodings.

This paper presents an efficient method for generating spatial constraints in dynamic environments. Building upon prior research, we extend the classical Reeds and Schumacher framework to address the challenge of navigating obstacles that change shape over time. Our solution consists of a two-step algorithm that leverages spatial relationships and optimization techniques to produce high-quality constraints with minimal points, thus enabling more efficient navigation in complex environments. We evaluate the proposed method against existing approaches in literature with an extensive benchmark suite, and demonstrate its superior performance and reliability. Furthermore, we integrate our constraints into a well-known motion planning algorithm, showcasing the resulting planner's exceptional performance in navigating diverse dynamic obstacles with reduced computational burden. Compared to its counterpart, our planner delivers up to 5 times faster planning times and achieves significant improvements in success rate and path quality. You can find the project code at https://github.com/UTexasRG/SpatialConstraints. Our method's video introduction is available at https://vimeo.org/35805492. Additionally, a comprehensive paper can be accessed at https://arxiv.org/doi/10.1007/978-3-319-26561-1_39. The project was initially published in 2016 at ICRA. This research proposes a visual relocalization technique that leverages a pre-built 3D surfel map as a reference. By utilizing both geometric and photometric information from the surfel map, our approach aims to achieve precise localization without requiring sequence-specific features to be learned. By combining a geometric and a photometric stream, our method generates a unified probability distribution that enables accurate localization. To optimize localization efficiency, we incorporate a multi-resolution strategy and demarcate search regions, thereby significantly reducing computational complexity. Comprehensive evaluations of both simulated and real-world datasets show that our method surpasses existing state-of-the-art visual relocalization techniques by achieving better localization results with faster processing speeds. For instance, our method can localize the IBVS dataset more than 10 times faster than current state-of-the-art techniques. Furthermore, our method's source code is publicly available on GitHub, and our method's performance is demonstrated in a related video. Nonetheless, our method has some inherent drawbacks, as it requires an initially accurate map to achieve successful relocalization, and the process of extracting both geometric and photometric descriptors can be computationally expensive. To address these limitations, future research could focus on developing more efficient feature descriptor learning and map-based initialization techniques. This involves identifying a particular finite set that generates the semifield. Furthermore, for finite harmonic mappings between tropical curves, the rational function semifield of the first curve can be expressed as a finite set of elements over the pull-back of the rational function semifield of the second curve. Finally, the rational function semifields of tropical curves associated with finite harmonic maps have explicit generators with respect to the pull-back of the tropical coordinate semifield. This note primarily focuses on measuring the speed of a conditioned process approaching its quasi-stationary equilibrium under specific assumptions regarding its distribution. In reverse, we establish that a conditioned process converging uniformly to a self-conservative, ergodic Markov process also attains a distinct quasi-stationary equilibrium, which it converges toward at an exponential rate across all initial distributions. Furthermore, we illustrate a corollary ergodic theorem under specific conditions. In conjunction, we prove that a conditioned process converging strongly to a self-conservative, ergodic Markov process does not necessarily attain a distinct quasi-stationary equilibrium. Instead, it may fail to converge strongly toward any quasi-stationary equilibrium. In support of this assertion, we generate a protocol that systematically constructs a specific class of Markov processes lacking quasi-stationary equilibria. This research reviews a global analysis of Type-II two Higgs doublet models (2HDM) 
combined with upcoming experimental results from colliders and constraints 
provided by theoretical interfaces and constraints from current particle 
physics data. Specifically, a global analysis of twelve $2\lambda$ $2HDM$ 
parameters is performed for the first time, incorporating results from the 
latest ATLAS and CMS vector boson fusion measurements. Our findings reveal how 
each parameter can be connected when incorporating all available data. We also 
assess the influence of various theoretical and experimental constraints, 
including experimental bounds on charged Higgs searches at LHC. Furthermore, 
a detailed comparison is made with four specific $2HDM$ scenarios: Type-I, 
Type-II, lepton-specific and flavor-specific models. Interestingly, when 
incorporating all data, our results demonstrate that twelve $2\lambda$ $2HDM$ 
parameters can be determined independently, with most of them offering better 
constraints than theoretical constraints related to vacuum stability and decays. 
Furthermore, future colliders, specifically HL-LHC, LHeC, SHiP, SHFC and 
HL-SPPS, are expected to contribute more to the precise determination of the 
$2HDM$ parameters by a factor of two compared to SPPS. We have further projected 
how future sensitivity may unfold at HL-LHC, LHeC, SHiP, SHFC and HL-SPPS, 
leading to the conclusion that precision measurement of $\sin^2 \theta_W$ at 
LHeC will have the greatest potential for contribution among all future experiments. 
Notably, our analysis shows that current particle physics data already provides 
the dominant constraints on the $2HDM$ parameters, with several parameters 
determined more effectively than theoretical limits related to the universality 
of couplings and Higgs characterizations. Furthermore, loop level calculations 
of Higgs decays at HL-LHC and future neutrino experiments will have the 
significant impact in determining several $2HDM$ parameters effective at TeV 
scale by an order of magnitude more effectively than current particle physics 
data. We have further projected how future sensitivity may unfold at HL-LHC,

We demonstrate through simulated molecular surface experiments that neuroevolutionary learning can independently design particles and temporal strategies for enhancing spontaneous assembly processes, based solely on the desired end properties and specified structural characteristics, and not relying on pre-existing understanding of the physical laws or possible material configurations. This algorithm can effectively pursue both goal-oriented and open-ended design approaches, enabling it to either produce a material with user-defined features or explore and discover new structures within a specified set of constraints. In this exploration mode, it delves into the range of possible materials and structures that can be formed rather than merely identifying those that are thermodynamically favored or achievable within a given timeframe. Furthermore, we show that over time, the structures produced by open-ended design are increasingly diverse in form and more likely to exhibit intricate spatial connections, and we develop an approach for establishing a quantitative definition of computational structural complexity. Our research indicates that the resulting assembly protocols can be interpreted as optimally controlled time-dependent transformation processes, and we investigate the relationship between these protocols' internal time structures (temporal hierarchies, linearity, abruptness, and reproducibility) and the resulting material self-organization patterns. Ultimately, we find that more complex structures tend to exhibit greater variety in spatial arrangements, higher spatial interconnectivity, and increased overall structural complexity. These findings provide new insights into the underlying principles of self-assembly and highlight the potential of neuroevolutionary learning to drive innovative material discovery and sophisticated self-organization strategies. They also raise significant implications for understanding the nature of computational structural complexity and the potential to develop more advanced assembly technologies in the future. Finally, we reflect on the ethical considerations and potential societal impacts of these emerging technologies. Specifically, we investigate the relationship between input forces and resulting flows in dimension d. This work shows that the stationary Navier-Stokes equation becomes unstable when the input forces decrease slowly with spatial frequencies for certain dimensions and types of flows, causing the solution map to diverge at zero. Conversely, we find that this divergence is not a concern when the input forces decrease rapidly, and we specifically identify cases where this is true for 3D and 4D systems. By resolving these competing outcomes, we have fully addressed the open question for systems in dimension d ≥ 4. Moreover, we have derived more detailed and quantitative insights into the relationship between input forces and flow stability by establishing the specific conditions under which this relationship holds. These insights include the discovery that for 3D systems, using forces that decrease rapidly enough can stabilize the stationary Navier-Stokes equation even when the input forces decrease slowly, and we have identified the maximum possible rate of decay for forces that contribute to stability. This result is even more remarkable when considering that such forces are still essentially low-frequency in nature. datasets and generate general word meanings, researchers are exploring new ways
to enhance model performance. The quality of these word meanings depends on how
often the words appear in the data, leading to the exclusion of rare or unknown
words in many cases. Dictionaries, which provide definitions for words, can help
fill this gap by including infrequent words in the model. Previous dictionary-
aided methods have primarily focused on incorporating word definitions directly
into PLMs, however this technique has shown limited success and requires extra
dictionary retrieval steps during inference. This paper introduces a new
method, called Dict-BERT, which integrates dictionary definitions into PLMs at
the training stage by adding two new tasks to the traditional masked language
modeling process. This results in improved token representations that better
reflect actual word meanings. Experiments conducted on GLUE and SQuAD have
verified the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving superior results and
natural-sounding word definitions. Our code is publicly available on
GitHub-at/Dict-BERT. Our research finds that integrating dictionaries into PLMs
yields more comprehensive word meanings that can further enhance downstream
application model performance. Moreover, Dict-BERT generates definitions with
accurate meaning, opening up applications in NLP tasks such as text summarization
and word replacement. Finally, by using word definitions to represent meaning,
the model is able to understand language complexities involving word sense and
infrequent word usage. Our study is the first to successfully incorporate
dictionary definitions into PLMs, resulting in notable improvements and
providing insights for future research. The Dict-BERT model and all related
resources are accessible through the link at the top of the citation list. A

In this context, we explore a privacy-preserving approach called federated learning that enables several entities to train a robust machine learning model without exchanging sensitive information about their data. Based on how the entities cooperate, FL can be categorized into two primary forms - horizontal and vertical FL. The former involves participants who collaborate using identical data attributes, while in the latter, the participants' datasets consist of different features which are essential for successful collaboration. Due to the implementation complexities of FL, vertical FL is commonly employed. Here, we demonstrate a potential vulnerability in the VFL implementation, specifically on popular libraries like TensorFlow, PyTorch, and Ring, which could compromise the security of training data. This means that an attacker can easily deduce the features and labels of a participant's data, thus threatening its data privacy. Furthermore, we also identify a potential adversary who can exploit this vulnerability by combining just a handful of participants, typically just a few. This threat effectively nullifies the presumed data security measures implemented by participants. To address this concern, we propose a potential solution by introducing multiparty homomorphic encryption, which can encrypt data from multiple parties, thus protecting the security of training data. For practical purposes, we also identify a critical challenge in implementing this solution, namely, how to achieve computationally efficient results. To address this concern, we introduce a novel algorithm, which demonstrates that it is possible to achieve efficient results by way of circuit decomposition. This algorithm demonstrates its potential by successfully training a model on the FMNIST dataset, which consists of 10,000 samples, and evaluating it on the test dataset with an accuracy of 0.9701, while using the Ring library. Our implementation of this algorithm takes approximately 9.9 seconds to train and showcases the possibility of implementing efficient homomorphic encryption for the real-world application of data collaboration and training without compromising data security through the use of vertical federated learning. We introduce a game-theoretic model, known as Smart City Defense Game (SCDG), which involves multiple agencies making strategic decisions about resource distribution to defend against attackers who adapt to their previous actions. Our research focuses on deriving Bayesian Nash Equilibria for both attacker-defense and defense-defense scenarios, and demonstrates the effectiveness of two resource allocation policies in resolving partial obligations and mitigating financial burdens. We also conduct comparative analysis and present the results in the form of graphical illustrations to facilitate easier understanding and interpretation. Our study contributes valuable insights to the decision-making processes of Smart City agencies by providing effective frameworks and strategies for coping with simultaneous socio-physical and cyber attacks. Furthermore, it acknowledges the inherent uncertainties and uncertainties-related-corrections inherent in Markov Perfect Equilibria, and highlights the practical implications of implementing these decision-making approaches. We hope that this work can inspire the development of more advanced game-theoretic models and decision-making techniques for multi-agency decision-making in the context of multi-layered Smart City environments, ultimately contributing to the advancement of public policy and resource management. Long document retrieval has been a longstanding hurdle in both reading comprehension and information retrieval. Recent pre-training models have shown promise in addressing this challenge, particularly in the retrieval and ranking stages of long documents. Nonetheless, issues persist when processing noisy documents, notably the labeling noise inherent in the dataset. 

Label noise stemming from labels' reliance on short, inaccurate samples of the full document can significantly impair the model's performance in long document ranking. In response, we've developed a novel approach to labeling retrieval datasets, incorporating bag sampling and group-wise loss to mitigate long document labeling noise. 

This scheme divides a paragraph into distinct bags, sampling a sequence of prompts within these bags to generate multiple labels for a single document, ensuring that the model learns to execute these prompts correctly across the entire document. We've also introduced a group-wise loss strategy to address long-tail classification by reducing the model's focus on the most prevalent labels in each group.

Our method demonstrates exceptional efficacy on the MS MARCO long document ranking dataset, yielding a top-8 rank in the NIST test for the first time, boasting a top-1 accuracy of 59.24%. Despite the exceptional performance of Graph Neural Networks in semi-supervised node classification, they face significant challenges when dealing with an extremely limited number of labels. The semi-supervised pseudo-labeling method is often employed to enhance training in such scenarios. Nevertheless, existing pseudo-labeling techniques have several shortcomings. Primarily, they rely on a large number of pseudo-labels to effectively train Graph Neural Networks, which is often impractical in situations involving a very small pool of labeled samples. Furthermore, even though they can generate pseudo-labels at a fast rate, the quality of these labels is subpar due to high uncertainties associated with them. We propose a unique pseudo-labeling strategy called informative pseudo-labeling (IPL), which is designed to work effectively even with a very small number of labels. IPL operates by using local neighborhoods around nodes in order to increase the accuracy of pseudo-labels by considering the collective annotations of neighboring nodes. We have theoretically demonstrated that combining multiple pseudo-labels generated using neighboring nodes leads to a significant reduction in their uncertainties, thus resulting in a smaller set of high-accuracy labels required to effectively train the model. We have conducted extensive experiments using various graph data sets to compare the performance of IPL, outperforming other competing methods such as Curriculum-Labeled, Adaptive-Labeled and Entropy Minimization methods. Notably, IPL has achieved an impressive 4% increase in performance over Curriculum-Labeled while using half the number of labels, and surprisingly, IPL has even outperformed the adaptive method while utilizing labels in a more efficient manner. Our study shows that IPL is capable of training resilient models across a wide variety of scenarios and conditions. The code for our method has been made publicly available at the following GitHub repository: https://github.com/666666666666/Informative-pseudo-labeling.

Additionally, further increasing the turning rate can cause a return to predictable, limited patterns of movement. By analyzing selected "b" values and "phi" angles, the autonomous entities are found to exhibit a combination of two distinct behaviors - either oscillating while remaining near their target, or else meandering through their surroundings - with the possibility of a third transition, into chaotic motion, for certain values of "phi". One of the widely applied optimization methods in machine learning is Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), which tackles optimization problems by iteratively selecting and computing gradients of small data subsets before updating the solution. When executed in parallel, SGD demands communication among involved processes at each iteration. Our innovation is a communication-optimizing approach for utilizing SGD to solve logistic regression. This strategy organizes computations into a pattern where communication is required only every $s$ iterations, as determined by the $s$ tuning parameter. By deriving theoretical bounds on operations count, data transfer rates, and latency, and accompanied by experimental findings, we demonstrate that the newly designed Communication-Avoiding SGD (CA-SGD) can reach speedups of up to $4.97$ on high-performance clusters, preserving the same convergence and accuracy as standard SGD. Our study is the first to provide an in-depth analysis of communication in SGD, leading to improvements in optimization algorithms' efficiency. Besides logistic regression, we successfully apply CA-SGD to linear SVM and Generalized Linear Group Lasso. Our software is openly accessible on GitHub at https://github.com/ksugimoto/ca-sgd. In polycrystalline and amorphous samples resulting from disorder-induced crystallization, we identify key findings that unintentionally facilitate the achievement of a chiral spin liquid in the triangular lattice $A_\textrm{II}$(\textit{Pt/SmFeO$_3$})$_4$ system, previously shown to be effectively chiral through lattice distortion. We find that regular polycrystalline synthesis yields numerous large grains interconnected by a limited number of crystal boundaries, creating closed pathways that foster chord effect-driven chiral order. We also find that amorphous samples synthesized using a conventional technique exhibit natural thermal stability over multiple cycles, demonstrating sufficient thermal history for the emergence of chiral order. We establish that controlled thermal treatment can stimulate phase transitions between chiral and nematic states due to external influences, and we identify the optimal thermal regime for each synthesis method to determine the effective effectiveness of these conventional techniques in producing samples conducive to a chiral spin liquid. These findings emphasize the considerable influence of synthesis techniques on material properties and establish polycrystalline and amorphous techniques as viable strategies for reaching compounds that would otherwise prove difficult to access. We begin exploring the sensory capabilities of these samples, a potential innovation that could stem from the emergence of a chiral liquid in these compounds. We anticipate that further research within this framework may lead to breakthroughs in the development of chiral spin liquids in general. We propose several potential applications of these samples in the future, including the establishment of chirality in non-chiral substances and potential connections to ferro/ferrimagnetism and superconductivity. Notably, the emergence of a chiral spin liquid in these samples facilitates a global-scale magnetic sensing on an large scale, an achievement previously considered as one of the biggest challenges in the field. We also prove that self-consistent condition-based and by-hand calculations in the J-Q model are equivalent to numerical dominant condition-based calculations and validate the J-Q model as the correct theoretical framework for understanding the phase behavior in the triangular lattice $A_\textrm{II}$ system, a natural outcome of previous model-based analyses on this system. We conclude by identifying a new triangular lattice system, \textit{Eu/MoO$_2$}$_4$, in which the phase behavior exhibits an opposing trend to that in the $A_\textrm{II}$(\textit{Pt/SmFeO$_3$})), serving as a natural reference point for ideal single-crystal samples

Future large-scale radio interferometers, aiming to detect 21\,cm signals across vast distances, may struggle with computing cross-correlations given traditional architectures, where the computational demand increases exponentially with the number of antennas involved. Traditional architectures, requiring the calculation of all antenna pairs, become impractical for arrays with many antennas. The introduction of the FFT-correlator architecture reduces the computational complexity, but its results are valid only when input data are evenly spaced. This requirement can no longer be met in large, planar arrays where antennas are placed irregularly on the surface. We propose a new calibration scheme that leverages FFT-correlators in large-scale radio interferometers with a regular antenna grid, eliminating phase errors and adding only logarithmically to the computational complexity, making it scalable for massive arrays. The new scheme can also determine antenna positions with high precision. Once the phase errors are calculated, we adjust the data accordingly using a per-dataset solution approach, spreading the errors out in a systematic manner across the data sets. The combination of the FFT-correlator with the per-dataset solution approach eliminates the computational barriers associated with large arrays. The per-dataset solution also facilitates the discovery of minor hardware irregularities, allowing for precise calibration of the hardware. The overall design, based on the FFT-correlator with the per-dataset solution approach, offers an attractive solution for future large-scale arrays, keeping the computational complexity at logarithmic scale relative to the number of antennas involved. The new architecture, applicable to all science cases covered in the CHORD project, offers the scalability needed for the large-scale observatories of the future. The science behind the large-scale projects, like the SKA, requires the calculation of the cross-correlations across the entire sky in order to solve the parameter estimation of the cosmological nature via the power spectrum. For several decades, the Markowitz framework has been used for in-depth portfolio analysis but sometimes at the expense of prioritizing other factors in portfolio construction. In this study, we utilize a variational autoencoder (VAE) in a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) to generate portfolios with reduced volatility, while maintaining the potential for increased returns. By employing the VAE to learn the underlying portfolio allocation space, we are able to introduce a novel approach to sampling and selecting portfolios that can be combined with any return expectation. This efficient sampling strategy allows for a substantial reduction of the number of portfolios needed for construction, by mapping these portfolios back to their original space and taking the expectation. We apply this framework in both simulated and real-world settings, focusing on small-cap and mid-cap stocks in the US market, demonstrating that our method can lead to successful risk-reducing strategies and potentially even boost returns. Our results indicate that our approach is viable for both machine-learned and observed return scenarios and can potentially accelerate the portfolio optimization process. A groundbreaking method using Bayesian neural networks assigns classifications to data with uncertain or noisy labels, which is particularly useful in a study on gamma-ray sources. The study involves over 500 3FGL objects, including blazars, pulsars, and other miscellaneous sources, with the latter two grouped as 'others'. Results from the analysis indicate that the majority of objects in the 'others' category can be distinguished from blazars with moderate certainty, but objects with less clear labels are more likely to be mixed, affecting the outcome. The implementation of Bayesian neural networks yields more reliable results and exhibits greater resistance to label noise compared to a traditional binary classification method. The study's findings enable the derivation of an accurate 'others' classification radius, which is set at 0.25 in terms of normalized score distance. The analysis also explores novel classification metrics that better account for uncertain labels and are more suitable for use cases, including improved recovery rates and enhanced score calibrations. The study's outcomes and analysis serve as a model for dealing with inherently uncertain data in the field of machine learning in the scientific community. Active participation and social connection are crucial components of any society, and technology plays a major role in facilitating these interactions through various online platforms. However, to truly promote social interaction and foster a sense of community, accessibility must be prioritized, enabling users with disabilities to engage with technology on an equal basis. The social media industry has begun to adapt to disability inclusion by introducing features such as accessible posting for users with visual impairments. Notwithstanding this progress, significant obstacles remain to creating accessible content on social media. To better understand this challenge, our research involved surveying social media users about the difficulties they encounter when attempting to create accessible content, and we identified both the hurdles they face and the opportunities available to overcome them. Our research has led to several key findings and recommendations for the social media industry, users with disabilities, and researchers, highlighting areas of improvement and offering potential solutions to further promote inclusion and equality. The study's results have been shared at an ACM accessible computing conference, and the associated data and code are available for further study and improvement. The research was grounded in the principles of the Accessible Authoring (or Content Authoring) framework. The framework consists of three key components: 1) creating content that is accessible to sensorimotor impaired users; 2) ensuring the content can be created in a format that is accessible to sensorimotor impaired users; and 3) promoting awareness and facilitating the inclusion of users with disabilities in content creation. The study was conducted through online surveys and interviews with representatives from the Microsoft Accessibility Internship Program, and the results were observed in three primary areas: 1) the accessibility of social media platforms; 2) the accessibility of content creation tools; and 3) awareness and education regarding accessibility and inclusion. The research team developed several key recommendations for each of these areas to promote inclusion and equality for users with disabilities on social media. The study concluded with a call to action for researchers, developers, and users with disabilities, and offered potential solutions to improve accessibility and inclusion in the future. In this paper, a new approach called tensor join is introduced for the integration of hypergraphs, by extending the concept of a join operation initially developed for graphs. This innovative method unifies two hypergraphs based on their common vertices, forming a new hypergraph, and is computed using a tensor representation that can be calculated through the singular value decomposition of a key matrix. Properties and examples of tensor join operations across different dimensions and sizes are demonstrated, showcasing its efficiency and computational feasibility. Furthermore, spectra-based methods for calculating the tensor join of hypergraphs are developed, providing accurate results even for large and complex hypergraphs. Finally, two data analysis applications using the tensor join operation are highlighted, illustrating its value in real-world scenarios. The implementation of the algorithms described in this paper can be accessed through a publicly available repository, utilizing the Python programming language. The results of our research show that the tensor join operation offers a valuable framework for the integration of hypergraphs. Additionally, spectra-based methods provide a useful alternative to other join operations for the analysis of hypergraphs. Finally, applying the tensor join operation to real-world data demonstrates its potential in the domain of data mining. In clinical trials for Alzheimer's and progressive diseases tracked with continuous data over time, the mixed model repeated measures approach often dominates. However, treating time as a categorical variable can introduce complications, particularly when appointments are missed or rescheduled due to events like the COVID-19 pandemic, which risks inducing bias. To address this limitation, a novel method employing natural cubic splines is presented to model time as a continuous variable and utilize treatment effect variations over time. The proposed method surpasses established models such as mixed model repeated measures and those relying on proportional treatment effects in real-world and simulation studies. Additionally, this method is showcased through its application in two actual Alzheimer's treatment trials. The associated R code is accessible via the package Alsplin, available on the CRAN repository. The supplementary materials can be found at the provided website.

A novel computational strategy called Action-CSA is introduced, enabling the global exploration of reaction pathways via optimization of the Onsager-Machlup action using conformational space annealing. Action-CSA is capable of sampling multiple reaction pathways without initial guesses and successfully captures both the most dominant pathway and a variety of alternative routes. Pathway diversity is facilitated by metropolis criteria and clustering, and the method's efficiency is enhanced through approximate calculations of the quadratic action using constraints. Action-CSA is demonstrated by identifying the dominant reaction pathway for alanine dipeptide and hexane in atomic detail, and the results are further validated through comparison with existing path sampling techniques and simulation-based continuous dynamics methods. The strategy is versatile, suitable for optimizing multiple reaction pathways without prior assumptions, and it can be adapted for parallel computing and Markov chain dynamics. Overall, Action-CSA presents a new way to understand complex chemical reactions by identifying stable states and exploring conformational space. The approach offers significant potential for investigating a wide range of dominant reaction pathways in realistic molecular systems. The strategy is available for public use on GitHub at https://github.com/MarkEastgate/Action-CSA under the Apache 2.0 open-source license. Lastly, the results highlight the practical significance of considering multiple reaction pathways in understanding and predicting the behavior of complex molecular systems. The pathway description also offers useful insights into designing experiments and evaluating existing simulation results, and it reveals the substantial influence of pathway selection on apparent thermodynamic and kinetic properties. The concept of dominant reaction pathways is therefore likely to play a central role in understanding and predicting the behavior of complex molecular systems in the future. In complex multi-robot systems, accurately navigating while avoiding potential collisions between robots is a significant challenge, largely due to the unpredictable movements of fellow robots. To tackle this, our method develops a data-driven strategy where each robot continually resolves a short-term optimization issue, incorporating constraints derived from observing safe approaches to targets taken by other robots that have encountered similar situations. Through a simplified data compression technique, our approach enables it to quickly access and solve for safe pathways to targets that have been encountered before. This enables seamless collaboration among robots with the same settings, ensuring their trajectories avoid one another while adhering to given targets. To maintain efficiency in processing, our method computes and executes the resulting commands in a timely fashion: upon receiving new information, each robot solves the optimization issue within a few seconds, leading to significant improvements over existing collision avoidance methods. Relative to other predictive control methods, our approach exhibits remarkable robustness in handling the unpredictable movements of fellow robots and yields substantially shorter computational times. Simulation results demonstrate that our method excels over other advanced techniques in terms of both performance and processing speed. Furthermore, our approach has been successfully tested on a real-world drone navigation application, with the drones successfully avoiding each other while completing tasks within a few seconds.
